sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology > Tone: 'From Köhler's material, it appears that ǁXʼegwi had a four-tone inventory.' (unsourced in the wikitext; the article's phonology cites Honken 2020 and Traill 1999). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1956. A Bushman Dictionary. American Oriental Series 41. New Haven: American Oriental Society. (SIII = 'batwa, Lake Chrissie, eastern Transvaal', D.F. Bleek's own pre-WWI field data)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction lists SIII = batwa of Lake Chrissie and notes Miss Bleek 'visited Lake Chrissie in the eastern Transvaal to sample that of the Batwa'. No statement on stress for SIII or any language; only a general remark under the letter a: 'Some variations in tone and length have been noted, doubtless others have not been heard and recorded.' Dictionary entries for SIII carry no stress marks or discussion.
